status.en: 231 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Lagos, Abuja and Kaduna.
status.nb: 231 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Lagos, Abuja og Kaduna.

summary.en: Gunmen continue to carry out lethal attacks across northern Nigeria, killing civilians in Plateau, shooting Islamic cleric Yahaya Masussuka dead in Katsina, and slaying at least 62 people in Binnari, Taraba, prompting mass displacement. Bandits targeted APC supporters ahead of a rally in Katsina, while kidnappers abducted six residents from the Millennium City estate in Kaduna. Armed escorts of the Nigerian Correctional Service fired warning shots during an assault in Rivers that resulted in one death. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Våpnede menn fortsetter å utføre dødelige angrep i Nord-Nigeria, dreper sivile i Plateau, skyter den islamske lærde Yahaya Masussuka i døden i Katsina, og dreper minst 62 personer i Binnari i Taraba, noe som fører til massefordrivelse. Banditter målrettet APC-tilhengere før et møte i Katsina, mens kidnappere bortførte seks innbyggere fra Millennium City-området i Kaduna. Væpnede eskorter fra Nigerian Correctional Service avfyrte advarselsskudd under et angrep i Rivers som resulterte i ett dødsfall. Konflikten førte til 1 486 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
